title: The Present Indicative Active — First Conjugation
subtitle: amō, amās, amat, amāmus, amātis, amant.
objectives: Conjugate first-conjugation verbs in the present indicative active.
Recognize the theme vowel -ā- as the marker of the first conjugation.
Translate simple sentences with first-conjugation verbs.
Understand that Latin verbs encode person and number in their endings.

sections.heading: The first conjugation
sections.body:
Latin verbs change their endings to show person (who is acting) and number (how many). The first conjugation contains verbs whose infinitive ends in -āre: amāre (to love), laudāre (to praise), vocāre (to call). The theme vowel is -ā-.

Present indicative active:
  amō — I love
  amās — you (sg.) love
  amat — he/she/it loves
  amāmus — we love
  amātis — you (pl.) love
  amant — they love

Cicero writes: tē laudō. — I praise you.
Caesar writes: hostēs oppugnant. — The enemies attack.
Ovid writes: puella amat. — The girl loves.

items.answer: vocō, vocās, vocat, vocāmus, vocātis, vocant
